item.title: Fukiware Falls: The 'Niagara of the Orient' on the Tone River — Guide
item.description: Fukiware Falls, sometimes nicknamed the ‘Niagara of the Orient’ for its wide, low, sweeping profile rather than sheer height, is formed where the Tone River — Japan’s second-longest river — has carved through volcanic rock into a dramatic gorge roughly 7 m deep and up to 30 m wide at points. Wooden viewing platforms and walkways let visitors take in the scene from multiple angles, with the churning white water especially striking after rainfall and framed by vivid maple foliage each autumn.

item.title: Minakami White-Water Rafting: Japan's Premier Rafting Destination — Guide
item.description: Minakami has established itself as one of Japan’s premier white-water rafting destinations, its stretch of the upper Tone River offering consistent, reliable rapids fed by mountain snowmelt through spring and summer. Numerous outfitters run guided rafting tours suited to a range of experience levels, from gentle introductions for first-time paddlers to more technical routes through faster water, with the surrounding gorge scenery — dramatic in spring’s fresh greenery and autumn’s colour — adding to the appeal beyond the adrenaline of the rapids themselves.

item.title: Tone River Wetlands: Reed Marshes on Japan's Second Longest River — Guide
item.description: The Tone River, Japan’s second-longest river, has played a vital historical role as a trade and transport artery for the Kanto region since the Edo period. Where it approaches the Pacific in Ibaraki, extensive reed marshes and wetlands line the lower river, supporting a range of birdlife and offering a quieter, more contemplative landscape than the region’s more visited attractions. The wetlands are especially atmospheric in late afternoon, when golden light catches the tall reeds along the waterway.
